description: The bar chart illustrates the module-level Giga FLOPs (floating-point operations) for three different attention mechanisms—grouped attention (g=3), patch attention (k=3), and feed-forward—across three stages of an Audio back-end Conformer model. The x-axis represents the three stages, labeled as Stage 1 (d=180, n=500), Stage 2 (d=256, n=250), and Stage 3 (d=360, n=125), with the corresponding model dimensions and number of layers indicated. The y-axis quantifies the computational cost in Giga FLOPs, ranging from 0 to 0.3. In Stage 1, the grouped attention mechanism (blue bar) exhibits the highest computational cost at approximately 0.28 Giga FLOPs, followed by the feed-forward (green bar) at around 0.14 Giga FLOPs, and patch attention (yellow bar) at approximately 0.13 Giga FLOPs. In Stage 2, the grouped attention (blue bar) again has the highest cost at about 0.17 Giga FLOPs, followed by the feed-forward (green bar) at approximately 0.14 Giga FLOPs, and patch attention (yellow bar) at around 0.11 Giga FLOPs. In Stage 3, the grouped attention (blue bar) has a cost of approximately 0.13 Giga FLOPs, the feed-forward (green bar) is slightly higher at about 0.14 Giga FLOPs, and patch attention (yellow bar) is the lowest at approximately 0.1 Giga FLOPs. The chart shows that grouped attention consistently has the highest computational cost across all stages, while patch attention has the lowest. The feed-forward component's cost is generally intermediate, with a slight increase in Stage 3 compared to the other stages.
